progress_update.summary: We reviewed the State Graph and Links RFC end-to-end, identified critical semantic gaps, and resolved the major ones. The biggest addition is the workflow returning→completed lifecycle where linked children block parent completion, guaranteeing frozen graphs are fully immutable. We also clarified the mutability contract (links as delegated write permission), separated link status updates from completion handlers, and added coherent tree cancellation and timeout semantics. Failure propagation was simplified to the minimal default (child failure updates link status, parent continues) with advanced strategies deferred.
progress_update.goal: Produce a solid, internally consistent RFC for State Graph and Links that covers the core semantics of links, workflow lifecycle with linked children, observability via SSE, and composition patterns. Success = the RFC can be handed to an SDK implementer and a runtime implementer with no ambiguity on the core model.
accomplished: Full review of all 5 RFC/design docs (state graph, process composition, channels, future ideas, repartition scope)
Resolved mutability contract: links are delegated write permission from object to runtime
Added workflow returning→completed lifecycle: linked children block parent completion, full graph freezes atomically
Added workflow tree cancellation (propagates cancel through links) and timeout semantics
Clarified completion handler execution: link status always updated by runtime, handlers queued as normal invocations
Simplified failure propagation: child failure updates link status, parent continues, no automatic propagation
Moved 5 open questions to 'Resolved Design Decisions' section
progress_update.now: User wants a design discussion (not yet added to RFC) about objects participating in the state tree as promises. Concept: a workflow spawns an object, the object acts as an interactive promise (user fills in data), then ctx.freeze() makes it immutable, unblocking the parent workflow. This extends the 'linked children block completion' model to objects.
next_steps: Design discussion: object-as-promise with ctx.freeze() semantics - how objects participate in workflow completion blocking
Wire protocol / journal entry specification for links (deferred until semantics stable)
Cross-partition link design sketch (deferred but acknowledged as common case)
Consider whether the Process Composition RFC should be updated or left as-is given the divergence
constraints: Focus on semantics first, implementation details later
State Graph RFC stands alone - don't merge with Process Composition RFC
Failure propagation strategies deferred to future RFC
decisions: Links are delegated write permission - the object authorizes the runtime to update link status on workflow completion
Workflow completion requires all linked children to complete (recursively) - the 'returning' state is the waiting phase
Result is not observable until full completion (not on return, on completion)
Completion handlers fire on completed (full graph frozen), queued as normal invocations
Child failure does NOT kill parent - link status updates, parent continues, application logic decides
Graph curation is load-bearing - unlinked children don't block completion
open_questions: Object-as-promise: can objects participate in workflow completion blocking via ctx.freeze()?
Should workflows have a default timeout or is no-timeout the default?
Link storage model: same column family as state or separate?
Returning state: should it be observable to SSE clients or hidden?
risks: The two RFCs (State Graph vs Process Composition) have diverging models - may confuse future readers
Cross-partition links are deferred but most cross-service links will be cross-partition
